research_question: What is the effect of iron-fortified condiments or seasonings compared with the same condiment without added iron on serum or plasma ferritin concentration in children and adults?
control_label: Unfortified condiment or seasoning (same condiment without added iron)
outcome_description: Serum or plasma ferritin concentration at end of intervention, measured in µg/L (ng/mL)
positive_direction: Higher serum or plasma ferritin concentration in the iron-fortified condiment group compared to the unfortified control group (favours fortification)
search_queries: iron fortified condiment seasoning ferritin randomized trial
iron fortification soy sauce fish sauce salt ferritin clinical trial
iron fortified seasoning condiment plasma serum ferritin controlled trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised or cluster-randomised controlled trials evaluating iron-fortified condiments or seasonings (e.g., fortified soy sauce, fish sauce, curry powder, salt, or other condiments) in children or adults
Comparison group receiving the same condiment or seasoning without added iron (or with other micronutrients added equally to both arms)
Quantitative reporting of serum or plasma ferritin concentration at follow-up or change from baseline
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, or study protocols)
No comparison between an iron-fortified condiment/seasoning and an unfortified condiment control (e.g., control received iron supplements or another fortified food)
Non-randomised designs, observational studies, animal studies, or laboratory/in vitro investigations
No quantitative outcome data on serum or plasma ferritin concentration enabling calculation of mean difference (means, SDs, SEs, or sample sizes missing)
moderators_to_extract: Type of condiment or seasoning (e.g., soy sauce, fish sauce, salt, curry powder)
Iron fortificant compound (e.g., NaFeEDTA, ferrous sulfate, ferric sodium EDTA)
Target population age category (children, adolescents, adults, pregnant women)
Intervention duration in weeks or months
Baseline ferritin level / iron deficiency prevalence
effect_size_note: Pool as mean difference (MD) in µg/L (equal to ng/mL) using a random-effects model. Extract end-of-intervention mean, SD, and n per arm. If only change from baseline is reported, use change scores for both arms. If multiple follow-up times are reported, use the last one. Convert all values to µg/L (e.g., pmol/L × 0.445). Convert SE to SD (SD = SE × √n). For cluster-randomised trials, adjust sample sizes using the design effect: 1 + (average cluster size − 1) × ICC.
